cells.tense: The ability to feel with someone is here today, and your own edges have not gone soft.
cells.act: hold your shape under the weight
cells.ask: Next time a mood from someone close comes at you, stay with it one breath past what's easy and keep your shape while it presses. Then say one plain sentence about what you noticed.
cells.core:
Someone close to you is in the middle of something, and you pick it up in your body before they've said a word. That part is working. Their state lands in you, and you don't disappear into it — you can be moved by what's happening to them and still know what you think, what you want, where you stop. You also see the whole shape of it: how the pieces fit, what's really going on under what they're saying.
The weight is real. Carrying it without stiffening is the work, and it's work you can do. So when it comes, let it land, keep your edge, and stay one breath further than you normally would. You'll find you can carry a lot and still be yourself on the other side. That's what grows from here.
cells.sheetLine: You can feel someone's weight and still keep your own shape.
cells.verb: feeling-with: letting another's state land and still knowing your own shape
cells.place: standing back far enough to see the whole arrangement while still inside it

cells.tense: You're already bracing for a future where everyone's feelings arrive at once and none of them can be set down.
cells.act: let the thing end that is already over
cells.ask: Whatever you're still carrying for someone — a worry, a role, an old offer to fix it — that has already run its course: let it end, mark the end plainly, and don't take it back up.
cells.core:
In the middle of all these people, the line between what's yours to feel and what's theirs has gone soft. You can't tell whose hurt is in the air, which is why every feeling turns into a job and every job turns into yours. What's on its way is being braced for before it gets here, and the bracing is heavier than any of it would be.
Something in this pile is already finished. A worry that's played out. A role you keep running from habit. A fix you offered that nobody is waiting on anymore. Ending it isn't coldness — it's the only way the warmth has somewhere to go. Let it actually end. Close it, and keep it closed. What's left after that is smaller and truer, and the people in it can reach you instead of reaching the load.
cells.sheetLine: You can't tell whose feeling is whose anymore.

cells.tense: You were in the middle of something with someone, and you're still standing at that door.
cells.act: adjust one dial a little, then stop
cells.ask: In an ordinary exchange, turn a dial a notch — an extra sentence, a question you'd normally skip, a true detail instead of the safe answer — then stop there and notice what came back.
cells.core:
Someone is there, and the room with them stays at the surface. You can still see the whole pattern of what passes between people — that part hasn't gone anywhere — but nothing is running toward anyone, and it hasn't for a while. Not coldness. More like the wire is there and carrying nothing.
Rebalancing is what's used here, and it moves by small turns, not by forcing a feeling you don't have. Nothing gets pushed into the starved place. Turn a dial a notch: an honest sentence where the easy one would go, a question you'd normally leave unasked, and then stop. Don't try to feel more than you do. Just shift it a little and watch what comes back — a word, a face, something small, or nothing yet. Tomorrow, again. Connection returns in increments, not in a lurch.
cells.sheetLine: You can see the whole thing and still feel none of it.

cells.tense: You're already giving the thing that moves people, and your account of it says you were only being practical.
cells.act: trace the pattern across the last few times
cells.ask: Set three recent moments side by side where something you did made a person's load lighter, and look at what they share — the same kind of move, the same point where you stepped in. Name that shape in one line, to yourself.
cells.core:
People leave you steadier than they arrived, and more than one has said some version of the same thing about it. You don't feel it happening. From the inside, it reads as competence, or efficiency, or just what anyone would do. But look at recent moments: the same move shows up again and again, the same point where you step in and shift things for whoever is sitting across from you. That's what they're picking up.
Stepping back is where this gets seen. Pull far enough away to look at the shape itself, apart from any one instance — that's how something returns to you when you can't feel it from inside. Notice the shape, say it once to yourself, and then stop. If someone names it, you don't have to argue with them. You can just let it be true.
cells.sheetLine: The thing they feel from you is real. You just don't feel it.

A reader could reasonably say 'I'm not numb, I'm just tired, and this isn't about people.' The sentence that serves me more than them is any version of 'you feel nothing' — cut everywhere, replaced with what is observable in the moment.
